info.name: PepperX
info.description:
PepperX exposes one namespace over several protocols. This collection covers the two HTTP surfaces:

- **REST** (baseUrl, default http://localhost:8000) - the complete native API, grouped by endpoint type.
- **S3** (s3BaseUrl, default http://localhost:8001) - the S3-compatible surface, grouped into Buckets and Objects.

A bucket is the same object as a container, so a value written over REST to {{container}} is readable over S3 in the bucket of the same name, and vice versa.

**Authentication.** REST is unauthenticated - it is backend infrastructure meant to sit behind a service that performs its own access control, so every REST request (including the DESTRUCTIVE ones) works against any node you can reach. S3 requests are signed with AWS Signature v4 from the s3* variables; PepperX accepts the signature rather than verifying it.

Set the variables on the collection, then start with **REST > Health > Server info**.

variable.description: Container name (also the S3 bucket name) used across the collection.
Object key, shared by REST and S3. URL-encode reserved characters for REST.
A request-history record ID, taken from the list endpoint.
S3 access key. A client affordance, not verified by PepperX.
S3 secret key. A client affordance, not verified by PepperX.
S3 region sent in the signature and returned by GetBucketLocation.

item.name: REST
item.description: The native PepperX REST API (port 8000) - the complete surface. It is unauthenticated by design, so every request works against any node you can reach, including the ones marked DESTRUCTIVE. Start with Health > Server info to confirm the endpoint is really PepperX. Uses the baseUrl, container, objectKey, and requestId variables.

item.name: Health
item.description: Identity and liveness. Call GET / first to confirm you are talking to a PepperX node.

request.description: Product name, version, and uptime. Use this to verify the endpoint is PepperX.
200 when the process is running.
Liveness for monitors. Reports the process only - it does not probe PostgreSQL or storage, so a node can answer healthy while its database is down.

item.name: Containers
item.description: Containers hold objects and map one-to-one onto S3 buckets. Names follow S3 bucket rules: 3-63 characters, lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.

request.description: Create a container. Returns 409 if the name is taken.
Paged list. Label and tag filters need the enumerate form.
The same listing with the query in a body, for filters too long for a URL.
One container, including its live object count and byte total.
200 if it exists, 404 if not.
Replaces the entire tag map. This is not a merge - an empty object clears all tags.

The container's cache configuration plus this node's live cache statistics (hit rate, resident objects and memory, evictions). A container created without a cache block defaults to caching enabled (LRU).

Replace the container's cache settings and apply them to the live cache. Reads are cache-first (a validated hit is served from memory with no lease), writes are write-through, deletes evict first. Policy is FIFO or LRU. MaxMemoryBytes 0 means no memory cap; MaxCacheableObjectBytes 0 means no per-object ceiling. Invalid input (e.g. EvictCount greater than MaxObjects) returns 400. A full rehydrate --mode Rebuild resets cache settings to defaults.

Assign or clear the container's RESP (Redis) database index. A Redis client that issues SELECT n with the assigned index addresses this container instead of the default resp{n}. The index is unique across containers (409 on conflict); a negative index is 400. Send {"Index": null} to clear the mapping. To be selectable the index must be within Resp.DatabaseCount (16 by default).

item.name: Objects
item.description: An object is one immutable extent: a payload plus labels, tags, and a freeform JSON metadata object. Keys travel as ?key= rather than in the path because they may contain slashes.

header.description: Base64 of a JSON document. Bounded by the server's header limit, 16 KiB by default - use the JSON envelope form for anything larger.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.
Return 409 instead of replacing an existing key.

request.description: Payload as the raw request body - the form to use for anything large, since it streams rather than being buffered. Metadata travels in headers.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.

request.description: Payload base64-encoded in a JSON body. Use when the metadata object is too large for a header, or the client cannot set custom headers. Costs about a third in transfer size and holds the payload in memory on both ends.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.

request.description: Raw payload bytes; metadata comes back in x-pepperx-* headers.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.

request.description: Partial read, answering 206 Partial Content.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.

request.description: Existence and metadata headers without the payload - the cheapest way to check a key.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.

request.description: Full metadata including labels, tags, and the freeform object, without transferring the payload.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.

request.description: Rewrites the extent preserving the payload, so the extent ID changes. Null means 'leave unchanged'; use ClearObject to remove the metadata object.
Paged list within one container.

item.name: Search
item.description: Label and tag filters are conjunctive: every listed label and every listed tag pair must match. There is no 'any of' - run separate queries and union the results.

request.description: Search one container by labels, tags, prefix, and creation window.
Search across every container; omit Containers to search all of them. Page by following ContinuationToken until EndOfResults - that is stable under concurrent writes in a way Skip is not.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Statistics, cluster membership, configuration, and rehydration.

request.description: Container and object counts, bytes stored, per-container rollups, volume capacity, metadata database size, and cluster nodes.
Node membership and liveness. A node counts as dead after Cluster.NodeDeadAfterSeconds without a heartbeat, 60 by default.
Non-secret configuration: protocol listeners, storage driver and directory, database location, node identity. The database password and S3 static keys are deliberately omitted.

Reconcile the metadata database against raw extent storage. Verify reports drift and changes nothing; Repair fixes it; Rebuild reconstructs the database entirely from storage. Always run Verify first - Rebuild reads every extent header on disk.

item.name: Request history
item.description: Every REST request this node served. This is what backs the dashboard's Request History view.

request.description: Paged list. Bodies are omitted here - fetch a single record for those.
One record in full, including headers and bodies. Bodies are truncated at the configured limit and flagged when they are.
Time-bucketed counts for charting. Empty buckets come back as zeros so a client need not fill gaps itself.
Delete one record.

query.description: Delete only records with this status.

request.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Bulk delete by filter, using the same parameters as the list. With no filter this deletes all retained history.

item.name: Cleanup
item.description: Destructive operations, kept last so the collection can be run top to bottom without deleting the container the earlier folders depend on.

query.description: Object key, URL-encoded. May contain slashes.

request.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Tombstones the extent, waits for in-flight read leases across the cluster to drain, then destroys the payload - so a read that began before the delete still completes.

query.description: Delete the container's objects along with it.

request.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Fails with 409 NotEmpty if the container still holds objects; force=true deletes them too, which is not recoverable.

item.name: S3
item.description: The S3-compatible surface (port 8001). Buckets map one-to-one onto PepperX containers, so a bucket here is the same container you see under REST. Requests are signed with AWS Signature v4 using the s3AccessKey / s3SecretKey / s3Region variables; PepperX accepts signatures rather than verifying them, and also allows anonymous access. Not implemented: multipart upload, versioning, ACLs, and lifecycle rules.

item.name: Buckets
item.description: Bucket-scoped S3 operations. A bucket is the same object as a PepperX container (one-to-one), so {{container}} names the bucket here.

request.description: ListBuckets. Returns every container as an S3 bucket.
CreateBucket. Subject to the container naming rules (3-63 lowercase alphanumeric or hyphen).
HeadBucket. 200 if the bucket exists, 404 otherwise.
GetBucketLocation. Returns the node's configured S3.Region.
ListObjectsV2. Supports prefix, delimiter, max-keys, and continuation-token query parameters.
GetBucketTagging. Returns the container's tags as an S3 TagSet.
PutBucketTagging. Replaces the container's tag set.
DeleteBucketTagging. Clears the container's tags.
DeleteBucket. DESTRUCTIVE. Fails if the bucket is not empty, matching S3.

item.name: Objects
item.description: Object-scoped S3 operations. {{objectKey}} is the key within {{container}}; an object written here is the same object visible over REST.

request.description: PutObject. Streams the body; the SDKs' AWS streaming-signature format is decoded before storage.
GetObject. Supports a Range header for partial reads.
HeadObject. Metadata and size without the payload.
GetObjectTagging.
PutObjectTagging. Replaces the object's tag set.
DeleteObjectTagging.
DeleteObject. DESTRUCTIVE.
DeleteObjects. DESTRUCTIVE. Batch delete; the body lists the keys to remove.

item.name: Multipart
item.description: S3 multipart upload: initiate, upload/copy parts, complete, abort, and list. Run Initiate first; it captures the UploadId into a collection variable. Capture each UploadPart response ETag into part{n}Etag before running Complete.

request.description: CreateMultipartUpload. Returns an opaque UploadId (captured into the uploadId variable by this request's test script).
UploadPart. The response ETag is the part's MD5; save it into a part1Etag variable for Complete.
UploadPartCopy. Copies a part from an existing object named by x-amz-copy-source (optionally a byte range via x-amz-copy-source-range).
CompleteMultipartUpload. Body lists the parts in ascending order with their ETags. Edit the body to match the parts you uploaded.
ListParts. Paginated via max-parts and part-number-marker.
ListMultipartUploads. Lists in-progress uploads for the bucket; paginated via max-uploads, key-marker, and upload-id-marker.
AbortMultipartUpload. Discards the staged parts.
